title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array Increasing
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of increment operations required to ensure each element is less than the next.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of increment operations required to ensure each element is less than the next. An increment operation increases any element by one. An array is strictly increasing if each element is smaller than the one following it.
constraints: One operation increments one array element by one.
Return the minimum operations needed to make the array strictly increasing.
hints: Each position only needs to exceed the finalized value immediately before it.
Leave a value unchanged when possible; otherwise raise it to previous+1.
Add the required increase and carry the adjusted value forward.
Any larger choice wastes increments and cannot help earlier positions, so the smallest legal value is greedily optimal at every step.
editorial: Any larger choice wastes increments and cannot help earlier positions, so the smallest legal value is greedily optimal at every step.

tests.explanation: Raise the second value to two and the third to three, costing three increments.
The cheapest increasing result is [1,5,6,7,8], requiring fourteen increments.
